lesson: Layer 22 attention was the best lead, but even the strongest tested subset [6,9,10,11] only dropped GSM8K by 9.21% and trivia by 2.72%, so it is still far from a gate-passing part.
Growing layer-22 MLP neurons from 10 to 40 did not scale well: GSM8K drop rose only from 0.74% to 1.15%, while control effects stayed tiny (<=0.21%).
The strongest MLP cluster tested, layer 27 top-40 neurons, looked math-relevant but was confounded: GSM8K dropped 7.67% and wiki_digits dropped 32.72%, so it was not math-selective.

Whole-block ablations were much stronger but too broad: layer 22 block dropped GSM8K 29.77%, trivia 34.90%, and wiki 13.54%; layer 27 block dropped GSM8K 14.09% but trivia 80.30%, showing poor selectivity.

Ranking by selective attribution was useful for finding candidates, but the top-ranked units often had very small individual effects; e.g. layer 22 top unit 5580 had rank_value 0.006628 and a single-unit ablation only moved GSM8K by 0.74% when grouped with 9 others.
Layer-22 attention was the real signal: heads [6,9,10,11] cut GSM8K gen accuracy by 47.6% (zero and mean) and 54.8–59.5% on held-out, while max control drop stayed under 3.0%.
Proxy NLL underestimated reasoning damage for attention: the same layer-22 4-head subset had only ~0.09 GSM8K score drop and small control effects, but generation accuracy fell by 0.476.
Selective MLP clusters in layers 21/22 were much weaker: growing from 256 to 512 units only reached 0.0–4.8% GSM8K gen drop, far below attention heads.
The compact 3-head subsets still validated well: [6,9,11] gave 42.9% gen drop on the main set and 45.2% on held-out, with max control drop 3.19%.
Validation was useful: all three candidate head subsets passed, and each beat random subsets with random_gen_drops often near 0.0–0.29 and percentile 1.0.
